facts.fact_text: On 2 April 2011 the first applicant attended an unauthorised opposition demonstration held at Fountains Square in Baku.
On 2 April 2011 the second applicant attended an unauthorised opposition demonstration held at Fountains Square in Baku.
The demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 was intended to be peaceful.
The demonstration held at Fountains Square on 2 April 2011 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
Upon arriving at Fountains Square at around 3 p.m. on 2 April 2011, the first applicant was arrested by police officers.
After his arrest, the first applicant was taken to the Nasimi district police office.
The first applicant was taken to the Nasimi district police office together with other participants in the demonstration, including M.H. and N.S.
After his arrival at the Nasimi district police office, the first applicant was placed in the exercise yard of the temporary detention centre of the Nasimi district police office.
The first applicant was placed in the exercise yard of the temporary detention centre of the Nasimi district police office together with other people who had been arrested, including M.H. and N.S.
The first applicant was allegedly beaten by S.N., who was the Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office.
The first applicant was allegedly beaten by a police officer called J.A.
The first applicant was allegedly beaten by a person wearing plain clothes whom the first applicant did not know.
According to the first applicant, S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) swore at the first applicant.
According to the first applicant, S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) kicked the first applicant in his abdominal area.
According to the first applicant, S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) punched the first applicant.
According to the first applicant, after S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) kicked him in his testicles, the first applicant lost consciousness owing to the severe pain.
According to the first applicant, despite his requests, he was not provided with the requisite medical assistance while in police custody.
The Government maintained that the first applicant had not been subjected to torture or inhuman or degrading treatment in police custody.
According to the first applicant, at around midnight on the day of his arrest (2 April 2011) he was taken to the Nasimi District Court.
According to the Government, the first applicant was taken to the Nasimi District Court at around 5 p.m. on 2 April 2011.
The first applicant stated before the Nasimi District Court that he was not guilty of disobeying the lawful order of a police officer.
The first applicant did not have any lawyer at the court hearing before the Nasimi District Court.
The first applicant insisted on being allowed to have a lawyer of his own choice at the court hearing before the Nasimi District Court.
The first applicant requested to invite witnesses to testify on his behalf at the court hearing before the Nasimi District Court.
The judge of the Nasimi District Court disregarded the first applicant's requests to have a lawyer of his own choice and to invite witnesses to testify on his behalf.
The hearing before the Nasimi District Court was brief.
The Nasimi District Court found that the first applicant had failed to stop participating in an unauthorised demonstration.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the first applicant under Article 310.1 (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Nasimi District Court sentenced the first applicant to eight days' administrative detention.

The Nasimi District Court relied on the testimony of police officer A.E., who testified that the first applicant had been attempting to hold an unauthorised demonstration and had continued his actions, disobeying a request to stop participating in the unlawful demonstration.

The Nasimi District Court relied on the testimony of police officer E.S., who testified that the first applicant had been attempting to hold an unauthorised demonstration and had continued his actions, disobeying a request to stop participating in the unlawful demonstration.
During the court hearing on 2 April 2011 before the Nasimi District Court, the first applicant complained that on that day he had been beaten at the police station.

During the court hearing on 2 April 2011 before the Nasimi District Court, the first applicant asked the court to facilitate the provision of the requisite medical assistance, but his request was ignored.
On 4 April 2011 the first applicant lodged an appeal with the Baku Court of Appeal.
In his appeal to the Baku Court of Appeal, the first applicant argued that his arrest had been unlawful.
In his appeal to the Baku Court of Appeal, the first applicant argued that his conviction had been unlawful.

In his appeal to the Baku Court of Appeal, the first applicant argued that the hearing before the Nasimi District Court had not been fair, in particular that he had not been allowed to have a lawyer of his own choice.
In his appeal to the Baku Court of Appeal, the first applicant argued that his procedural application to call witnesses to testify on his behalf had been dismissed by the Nasimi District Court.
In his appeal to the Baku Court of Appeal, the first applicant complained of ill-treatment.
In his appeal to the Baku Court of Appeal, the first applicant stated that he still felt unwell and had not received the requisite medical assistance.
On 8 April 2011 the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the first applicant's appeal.
The Baku Court of Appeal held that the first applicant had had a State-appointed lawyer at the first-instance court (Nasimi District Court).
The Baku Court of Appeal held that the first applicant's ill-treatment claims had not been proved.
On 6 April 2011 the first applicant lodged a complaint with the Nasimi District Court under the procedure for judicial review of prosecuting authorities' actions or decisions.
In his complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the first applicant relied on Articles 3, 5, 6, 11, 13 and 14 of the Convention and complained regarding his ill-treatment on 2 April 2011.
In his complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the first applicant complained regarding the unfairness of his conviction.
In his complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the first applicant complained regarding the violation of his freedom of assembly.
In his complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the first applicant complained regarding discrimination against him on the basis of his political views.
By a decision of 12 April 2011, the Nasimi District Court refused to admit the first applicant's case.
By a decision of 12 April 2011, the Nasimi District Court sent the first applicant's complaint to the Nasimi district prosecutor's office, claiming that the latter had the authority to consider it.
On an unspecified date in April 2011 the first applicant applied to the Baku prosecutor's office, requesting that a criminal investigation into the matter of his alleged ill-treatment be instituted.
According to a forensic report dated 15 April 2011, there was an abrasion on the first applicant's left calf caused by a blunt object.
According to the forensic report dated 15 April 2011, the abrasion on the first applicant's left calf could have been inflicted on 2 April 2011.
By a decision of 28 April 2011, the Nasimi district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case regarding the first applicant's alleged ill-treatment.

The Nasimi district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case on the grounds that the first applicant's beating by S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) had not been proved.

The Nasimi district prosecutor's office mainly relied on the findings of an inquiry conducted by the Nasimi district prosecutor's office into a similar complaint of ill-treatment from M.H., who had been detained with the first applicant on 2 April 2011.

Within the framework of the investigation into M.H.'s complaint, the first applicant, when questioned as a witness, gave testimony about being ill-treated by S.N. and other officers while in police custody.
Within the framework of the investigation into M.H.'s complaint, M.H. gave testimony about being ill-treated by S.N. and other officers while in police custody.

Within the framework of the investigation into M.H.'s complaint, N.S., who had been detained with the first applicant on 2 April 2011, gave testimony about being ill-treated by S.N. and other officers while in police custody.
S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) denied any involvement in the first applicant's case, stating that he had not been at the Nasimi district police office at the material time.
Police officer V.M. stated that the first applicant had not been detained in the temporary detention facility and had not been beaten.
Police officer M.R. stated that the first applicant had not been detained in the temporary detention facility and had not been beaten.
Police officer E.S. stated that the first applicant had not been detained in the temporary detention facility and had not been beaten.
Police officer A.E. stated that the first applicant had not been detained in the temporary detention facility and had not been beaten.
Police officer E.S. added that the injury on the first applicant's leg might have been caused during his arrest, when he had resisted being put in the police car.
In an appeal of 31 May 2011 filed with the Nasimi District Court against the decision to refuse to open a criminal case, the first applicant reiterated his previous complaints.
In his appeal of 31 May 2011, the first applicant pointed out that his forensic examination had taken place so long after the event that most of the injuries on his body had disappeared.

In his appeal of 31 May 2011, the first applicant pointed out that the Nasimi district prosecutor's office had not identified the precise circumstances leading to his injury, in particular the place and time that his injuries had been inflicted.

In his appeal of 31 May 2011, the first applicant pointed out that he had not been called to testify, but his witness statement in M.H.'s case had been used instead, and no separate investigation into his complaint had been conducted.
On 21 June 2011 the Nasimi District Court held that the Nasimi district prosecutor's office's decision of 28 April 2011 to refuse to open a criminal case had been lawful.
The Nasimi District Court stated that the first applicant's complaint had been added to the investigation into M.H.'s similar complaint stemming from the same facts.
The Nasimi District Court stated that the relevant investigative actions had also been carried out in respect of the first applicant.
By a judgment of 14 July 2011, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the first applicant's appeal of 30 June 2011.
By a judgment of 14 July 2011, the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 21 June 2011.

At around 2 p.m. on 2 April 2011, while the second applicant was chanting during the demonstration at Fountains Square, four police officers approached him and twisted his arms behind his back in order to put him in a police car.
S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) allegedly knew the second applicant from previous demonstrations.

S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) insulted the second applicant and twisted his arm even more, saying to the police officers, "You should not twist [his arms], but break them, like this".
In response to S.N.'s twisting of his arm, the second applicant shouted out because of the pain.
Under S.N.'s orders, police officers beat the second applicant with truncheons.
The second applicant lost consciousness and lay on the ground for several minutes after being beaten with truncheons.
After the second applicant regained consciousness, the officers dragged him to a police car and took him to the Sabail district police office.
While in police custody at the Sabail district police office, the second applicant requested a medical examination and assistance, but his request was refused.
The second applicant was reprimanded for participating in a public assembly under Article 298 (violation of the rules on holding public assemblies) of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant was released at around 5 p.m. on 2 April 2011.
On 2 April 2011 the second applicant complained to the Sabail district prosecutor's office that he had been beaten and insulted during his arrest as a result of being an opposition member.
On 2 April 2011 the second applicant requested that criminal proceedings be instituted by the Sabail district prosecutor's office.
A forensic report dated 4 April 2011 stated that the second applicant had a bruise on his left arm.
The forensic report dated 4 April 2011 stated that the bruise on the second applicant's left arm could have been caused on 2 April 2011.
The second applicant sought medical assistance at a medical centre, which provided him with outpatient treatment.
According to the second applicant's medical records of 5 April 2011, issued by the medical centre, the second applicant had contusion of the soft tissues of his left upper arm and thorax.
According to the second applicant's medical records of 5 April 2011, the second applicant had thoracic bruising.
According to the second applicant's medical records of 5 April 2011, the second applicant had haemarthrosis of his right elbow joint.
The second applicant was prescribed outpatient treatment, including a sling for his left upper arm and medicine.
The medical records of 5 April 2011 stated that the second applicant was experiencing chest pain while breathing.
The medical records of 5 April 2011 stated that the second applicant had a haematoma and bruising on his upper arm, and that his upper arm's functions were limited.
The second applicant submitted the medical records of 5 April 2011 to the Sabail district prosecutor's office.

The second applicant submitted to the Sabail district prosecutor's office photos of him taken during the demonstration, which had been published in the 24-25 April 2011 issue of the Azadlig newspaper, and in which S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) and other police officers could be seen twisting his arm.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office questioned four police officers who had taken part in the second applicant's arrest.
S.N. (Deputy Head of the Nasimi district police office) denied the ill-treatment allegations against the second applicant, stating that he had not twisted the second applicant's arms.
Police officer A.R. claimed that he had not used physical force against the second applicant during his arrest, and that S.N. had not twisted the second applicant's arms.
Police officer V.S. claimed that he had not used physical force against the second applicant during his arrest, and that S.N. had not twisted the second applicant's arms.
Police officer A.A. claimed that he had not used physical force against the second applicant during his arrest, and that S.N. had not twisted the second applicant's arms.

Police officer A.A. mentioned that the injury to the second applicant could have been inflicted when the second applicant had resisted the police by pushing them and hitting a police car with his hands.
By a decision of 5 May 2011, the Sabail district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case regarding the second applicant's alleged ill-treatment.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office found that there was no evidence that the second applicant had been beaten by police during his arrest.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office relied mainly on the statements of the police officers in refusing to open a criminal case.

The Sabail district prosecutor's office held that the bruise on the second applicant's arm mentioned in the forensic report had been caused when the second applicant had demonstrated resistance to the police.
On 3 June 2016 the second applicant lodged a criminal complaint with the Sabail District Court against the Sabail district prosecutor's office's refusal to open a criminal case.

In his complaint to the Sabail District Court, the second applicant complained that the Sabail district prosecutor's office had failed to conduct an effective investigation into his ill-treatment complaints.

In his complaint to the Sabail District Court, the second applicant pointed out that the Sabail district prosecutor's office had relied on the testimonies of witnesses who had denied that S.N. had twisted his arms, while the photos he had submitted proved the contrary.

In his complaint to the Sabail District Court, the second applicant pointed out that the decision to refuse to open a criminal case was silent as to his other injuries confirmed by the medical records of 5 April 2011.
On 13 June 2011 the Nasimi District Court dismissed the second applicant's complaint, finding the investigator's decision to refuse to open a criminal case lawful.
The Nasimi District Court's decision of 13 June 2011 was silent as to the second applicant's specific complaints.
In an appeal of 16 June 2011, the second applicant reiterated his previous complaints regarding his alleged ill-treatment.
On 24 June 2011 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 13 June 2011 as lawful.
On 8 August 2014 criminal proceedings were instituted against Mr I. Aliyev, who represented the second applicant before the Court.
On 8 August 2014 the investigating authorities seized a large number of documents from Mr I. Aliyev's office, including all the case files relating to the ongoing proceedings before the Court.
On 9 August 2014 the investigating authorities seized a large number of documents from Mr I. Aliyev's office, including all the case files relating to the ongoing proceedings before the Court.
The seizure of documents from Mr I. Aliyev's office is referenced in the case of Aliyev v. Azerbaijan (nos. 68762/14 and 71200/14, 20 September 2018).
The case file relating to the present application was seized in its entirety from Mr I. Aliyev's office on 8 and 9 August 2014.

On 25 October 2014 the investigating authorities returned to Mr I. Aliyev's lawyer a number of the case files concerning the applications lodged before the Court, including the file relating to the present application.
